channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Maldon MP warns Hammonds Farm garden community could clog the A414 into town
item.description: Sir John Whittingdale has written to the planning inspector examining Chelmsford's Local Plan, saying the 3,000-home scheme would leave Maldon and Heybridge with worse congestion and few other routes.

item.title: Anglia Ruskin University seeks voluntary redundancies to cut staff bill by 10%
item.description: The university, which has campuses in Chelmsford plus Cambridge and Peterborough, spends about £150m a year on its workforce, the BBC reports.

item.title: Almost half of Stansted Airport passengers now arrive by train, bus or coach
item.description: More than 13.5 million people used public transport to reach London Stansted Airport over the past 12 months, the Bishop's Stortford Independent reports.

item.title: Inquest opens into death of Chelmsford boy, 2, who fell from Cyprus hotel window
item.description: Jaxon Foster died from multiple severe injuries on the first day of a family holiday in July, Essex Coroner's Court has heard.

item.title: Harlow man admits drug-driving on Southern Way and is given interim ban
item.description: Perry Brown, 38, of Long Banks, Harlow, pleaded guilty at Chelmsford Magistrates' Court to driving with cannabis in his blood above the legal limit.

item.title: Thurrock Council plans to save £995,000 as fewer families wait in emergency housing
item.description: Thurrock Council says the number of households it has placed in temporary accommodation is now falling by about 15 a month, after three years of steady rises.

item.title: Broomfield, Southend and Basildon hospital patients told to keep appointments as Microsoft email recovery continues
item.description: Microsoft says its email service is approaching normal levels after the global outage, but some messages are still arriving late.

item.title: Basildon Council forms fly-tipping task force after clearing 1,696 dumps in six months
item.description: Hotspots across Basildon borough will be targeted first, with surveillance, intelligence gathering and faster clean-ups, Basildon Today reports.

item.title: Former PC who saw cyclist heading into traffic before fatal A130 crash would have been sacked, hearing rules
item.description: A misconduct hearing chaired by Essex Police Chief Constable Rachel Nolan found Nicholas Davies did not stop, turn round or report the rider he had seen in Chelmsford.

item.title: Dover man, 83, charged with indecent assault in Harlow dating back to 1974
item.description: An 83-year-old man from Dover in Kent will appear at Basildon Crown Court in December over an alleged offence in Harlow more than 50 years ago.

item.title: Essex football and cricket clubs to lead year-long push on men's mental health
item.description: Essex County Council is funding the Colchester United, Southend United and West Ham United community foundations, with cricket partners, to reach men through sport across the county.

item.title: Braintree Town beaten 2-0 at Salisbury despite facing ten men after half-time
item.description: The Braintree side had an extra man for the whole second half in Wiltshire but could not find a goal in the National League South.

item.title: Maldon council agrees to buy two plots at Langford to protect wildlife habitat from inappropriate use
item.description: Maldon District Council will try to buy two parcels of land at Langford, near Maldon, sold at auction in 2025, and can pay up to 10% above an independent valuation to secure the deal.

item.title: New rules for licensed pet and animal businesses across Basildon borough adopted until 2031
item.description: Basildon Council has formally adopted an Animal Activity Licensing Policy and Animal Charter for 2026 to 2031, replacing its old Animal Welfare Charter after a public consultation.

item.title: Air ambulance downwash seriously injured woman filming its take-off near Southend Airport, report finds
item.description: Accident investigators say the Essex & Herts Air Ambulance crew could not see the woman behind a hedge in Southend and flew on unaware she had been hurt.

item.title: Partially blind after eye cancer, Felix is now studying music at Colchester Institute
item.description: The teenage pianist told BBC News that music carried him through his illness.

item.title: Westcliff construction insurance specialist Blackhawk bought by Clear Group
item.description: Blackhawk Insurance Services in Westcliff-on-Sea, Southend, is now part of a Goldman Sachs-backed broking group, with the price kept private.

item.title: Witham man, 21, jailed for 12 months over drugs and phones package thrown into HMP Chelmsford
item.description: The Witham man admitted conspiring to get cannabis, tobacco and mobile phones over the wall of the Chelmsford prison, and was sentenced at Chelmsford Crown Court.

item.title: Police ask Harlow drivers to look out for missing William Knight and his white Seat Ateca
item.description: Essex Police are concerned for the 30-year-old and want anyone who sees him or the car to call 999.

item.title: Waltham Abbey man banned for a year after cannabis drug-driving in Epping
item.description: Stuart Thurgood, 44, of Homefield, Waltham Abbey, admitted driving a Nissan in Epping with cannabis in his blood above the legal limit.

item.title: Michael Rosen performs for more than 300 Harlow primary pupils at the Playhouse
item.description: Former children's laureate Michael Rosen brought his stories to schoolchildren in Harlow as part of Essex County Council's events for the National Year of Reading.

item.title: Home Office bypasses Braintree council in bid to keep Wethersfield asylum centre open past April 2027
item.description: Braintree District Council is taking legal advice and says it wants the former RAF airbase, which has housed asylum seekers since July 2023, closed as soon as possible.

item.title: No direct summer flight from Stansted to Florence once British Airways leaves the airport
item.description: British Airways CityFlyer is pulling out of the Uttlesford airport after the 2026/27 ski season, but Ryanair will keep flying to Bergerac, Nice, Olbia and Palma.

item.title: Southend publishes three-year SEND plan after inspectors call for improvements
item.description: Better education, health and care plans and quicker access to neurodevelopmental support are among the aims of the Southend SEND Partnership's new action plan.

item.title: Ten-man Dagenham & Redbridge knock Tilbury out of the Essex Senior Cup
item.description: The Thurrock side, short of several players through cup-tie rules and absences, bowed out of the county competition in the fourth round.

item.title: Chadwell St Mary gets a Tesco Express on Defoe Parade
item.description: The new convenience store in Chadwell St Mary, Thurrock, has a bakery, a Costa coffee machine, a parcel locker and parking.

item.title: Thurrock crackdown on uninsured drivers takes 36 cars off the road in a single day
item.description: Officers in Thurrock teamed up with the Motor Insurers' Bureau for a one-day push against drivers with no cover.

item.title: Harlow RSPCA branch wins £10,000 to keep its animal welfare clinic open for longer
item.description: RSPCA Stort Valley, which runs a subsidised animal welfare advice centre at The Stow in Harlow, is one of five small charities sharing a £50,000 giving pot from the job board CharityJob.

item.title: Burnham-on-Crouch signs friendship pact with Carpathian town of Yaremche
item.description: Burnham-on-Crouch Town Council has become the first in Essex to twin with a Ukrainian community, linking the River Crouch town with Yaremche in the Ivano-Frankivsk region.

item.title: Christmas breakfast, market and Santa's grotto planned for Jaywick Sands at the Sunspot
item.description: Tendring District Council is inviting families in Jaywick Sands to a day of festive events at the Sunspot business centre in Brooklands.

item.title: Four pieces of council land in Tilbury put up for sale, including nine acres off Parker Avenue
item.description: Thurrock Council will consider objections to selling the Tilbury plots if they are lodged by 5pm on Friday 27 November 2026.

item.title: Colchester's Shrub End sports centre could get two new floodlit 3G pitches under £2m-plus plan
item.description: Colchester City Council and Colchester United Community Foundation have applied for planning permission to expand the Shrub End Community and Sports Centre, with the Football Foundation paying most of the cost.

item.title: Chelmsford roads operation ends in 19 arrests and suspected fake cigarettes seized
item.description: Essex Police's Operation Limit stopped drivers across the Chelmsford area and turned up crimes that had nothing to do with driving.

item.title: Batteries thrown out with household rubbish blamed for Colchester bin lorry fire
item.description: A bin lorry caught fire in Colchester, with the blaze put down to batteries that had been thrown away in household waste.

item.title: High tides prompt two flood warnings along the coast around Clacton
item.description: Parts of the Tendring coastline around Clacton-on-Sea are at risk of flooding from high tides, according to the Daily Gazette.

item.title: Tilbury youth zone on track for 2027 as charity warns of isolated generation
item.description: Building work continues on the OnSide Youth Zone in Tilbury, which will offer climbing, music production, fitness and affordable hot meals for Thurrock's young people.

item.title: Interactive artwork about living with MS and Parkinson's goes on show at Tilbury library
item.description: Thurrock dance charity CoDa has brought its Beyond the Darkness installation to Tilbury Library and Hub until Monday 7 December.

item.title: Six-vehicle M25 crash between the M11 and Waltham Abbey brings hour-long delays to morning rush
item.description: Two of the four anticlockwise lanes near Waltham Abbey had reopened after the pile-up, with Essex Police saying nobody was reported hurt.

item.title: Commissioner gives Essex residents until 25 November to have a say on police and fire funding for 2027/28
item.description: Roger Hirst, the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner for Essex, has extended his precept survey by two weeks after more than 750 responses.

item.title: Agency nurse told Colchester care home colleague he would 'kill' his whole family, panel finds
item.description: A Nursing and Midwifery Council panel found Rupesh Patel, 40, was drunk on a night shift at The Oaks care home in Colchester when he threatened a colleague, and he is set to be struck off.

item.title: Developer appeals over lack of decision on 910 green belt homes at Billericay's Foots Farm
item.description: Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee was asked to say how it would have decided the Great Burstead scheme, after an appeal was lodged because no decision had been made. Officers backed the plan, which offers more than £20 million in contributions.

item.title: Basildon councillors confirm refusal of 175 green belt homes at Little Burstead
item.description: Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee agreed the formal grounds for turning down homes west of Tye Common Road, near Billericay, going against officers' advice to approve.

item.title: Tendring councillors to vote on sending Local Plan for 1,069 homes a year to a government inspector
item.description: Tendring District Council's local plan committee meets on 17 November to decide whether to recommend submitting the plan, with Kirby Cross, Brightlingsea, Bradfield and Frinton sites drawing most objections.

item.title: Maldon scraps area planning committees and councillor call-in as new national rules take effect
item.description: Maldon District Council now has one 13-member Planning Committee, with most applications decided by officers under a new national scheme of delegation.

item.title: Maldon's share of the halted Mid Essex unitary council set-up costs put at about £26,000
item.description: Maldon District Council councillors have asked for a full breakdown, including officer time, of spending on the Mid Essex council plan before the government paused the Essex shake-up.

item.title: Hanningfield among England's most depleted reservoirs as Essex hosepipe ban enters fourth month
item.description: Hanningfield and Abberton, which supply much of mid and south Essex, held 37% of their capacity on 10 November, below average for the time of year, Essex & Suffolk Water says.

item.title: Suspected drug-drivers in Essex barred from driving for up to six weeks while police investigate
item.description: Essex Police says it is one of the first forces in the country to use bail conditions this way, as drug-driving arrests across the county keep rising.

item.title: Senior doctors' walkout that threatened Harlow hospital appointments is paused for pay talks
item.description: Consultants at Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow and across England will no longer strike later this month after the British Medical Association paused action to negotiate with the government.

item.title: Purfleet grandmother says rats are still keeping her family out of their Chieftain Drive council home
item.description: A Thurrock Council tenant in Purfleet says her family cannot move back in, while a ward councillor has asked the council for an action plan with timescales.

item.title: Frosty night for Essex, with Chelmsford forecast to drop to -3C
item.description: Clear skies after a sunny day mean temperatures are falling quickly this evening, so expect frozen windscreens first thing on Saturday.

item.title: Roper twins back at the University of Essex after double Commonwealth Games bronze for Wales
item.description: The Ipswich-born gymnasts won their medals within an hour of each other in Glasgow and are now back studying at the Colchester campus.

item.title: Chelmsford MP says Broomfield Hospital trust's recovery plan is moving too slowly
item.description: Marie Goldman wants clearer reporting on how the intensive NHS programme for Mid and South Essex will be judged, while the trust says waiting lists are already falling.

item.title: Pedestrian suffers potentially serious leg injury at Harlow crossing as police seek white or silver car
item.description: Essex Police say the car is reported to have gone through red lights at the Old House Croft crossing near Burnt Mill School in Harlow on Halloween evening and then left the scene.

item.title: Chelmsford Christmas lights to be switched on after a day of festive entertainment
item.description: Chelmsford city centre's Christmas lights switch-on is set for a Sunday, rounding off a full day of festive entertainment, Chelmsford City News reports.

item.title: Colchester curry house takes national Restaurant of the Year title
item.description: A Colchester Indian restaurant has been named Restaurant of the Year at the National Curry Awards.

item.title: Forecasters tip Harlow Conservatives to tighten grip on council next May, with Labour down to six seats
item.description: A seat-by-seat model of next year's Harlow District Council elections gives Reform UK nothing and leaves the Conservatives with a bigger majority.

item.title: Writtle restaurant Pakwaan is the only Essex name in national Indian food guide's top 100
item.description: Pakwaan Indian Punjabi Cuisine on Bridge Street, Writtle, near Chelmsford, made the British Indian Good Food Guide's 2026 selection.

item.title: Southend Hospital becomes first in Essex to win Sophie's Legacy award for looking after children's families
item.description: Southend Hospital's Neptune children's ward now provides meals for parents staying with their child and play specialists seven days a week.

item.title: Colchester United's home game with Fleetwood Town switched to Sunday 20 December
item.description: The League Two match moves back 24 hours so Fleetwood can recover from their Carabao Cup quarter-final against Everton.

item.title: Brentwood centre for rape and sexual assault survivors reopens after refit with new aftercare rooms
item.description: The Essex Sexual Assault Referral Centre, paid for by the county's police commissioner with Essex Police, stays in the county so survivors need not travel elsewhere.
